gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed new diagnosis of GBM according to updated World Health Organization (WHO) classification criteria.

candidate_evidence.quote: [DRUG] Concurrent Chemotherapy (Temozolomide) (other names: TMZ, Temodar): 75mg/m\^2 x 42 days (concurrent chemotherapy with radiation).

The primary protocol objective is to assess the impact of substituting pulsed reduced dose radiotherapy (pRDR) for standard radiation therapy in the upfront treatment of glioblastoma (GBM) on disease progression.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed new diagnosis of GBM according to updated World Health Organization (WHO) classification criteria.

role_evidence.quote: [DRUG] Concurrent Chemotherapy (Temozolomide) (other names: TMZ, Temodar): 75mg/m\^2 x 42 days (concurrent chemotherapy with radiation).

[DRUG] Adjuvant Chemotherapy (Temozolomide) (other names: TMZ, Temodar): Starting no sooner than 4 weeks after completion of chemoradiation, 150-200mg/m\^2, days 1-5 of 28-day cycle, for minimum of six cycles and up to 12 cycles.

source_quote.quote: All patients with sufficient tissue must have had tissue submitted for O6-Methylguanine-DNA Methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation determination prior to enrollment.

coder_notes: Single-arm trial testing pulsed reduced dose-rate radiotherapy (device/radiotherapy); standard temozolomide given as in Stupp regimen with unchanged standard dose, so no pharmacological candidate. Temozolomide listed twice because it is registered as two interventions (concurrent and adjuvant). MGMT: tissue must be submitted for determination but no MGMT status is required to enter, so not coded as eligibility.
